column1: # the subject in the .rxt subject-escape vocabulary. The byte patterns are lane iterdes's targeted
# set (docs/design/findall_iter/sem/targeted.tsv) plus the retry shapes the
# design names (\K, lookaround, anchors, compound splits); the utf8 groups
# carry ill-formed subjects, alone and under -futf-check. `a\x80a` and
# `\xc3\xa9\x80a` put a stray continuation byte right after a non-empty
# match (K75's aligned end, S1300's witness: findall_iter.md §6.8 S923); they
# ride every utf8 group that can report a non-empty match.
# >= 1 entry (S1311's witness, libpcre2 answers the rest), subjects with >= 63
# matches (the seventh RX_FOREACH fill asks 64: Fcount's floor), and the
# 3- and 10-group patterns the ASan cells build with -DRX_FOREACH_PAIRS=8
# (kmax 2 for S1317; a refusal past the buffer).
# The bare `\G` on the DFA: an empty match at n ends the iteration (the STEP's
# past-the-end test, lane i2build; S1321's witness).
